correctness.rationale: Direct reduction of the exact source update yields affine reversible self-loop random walk with signed endpoint current. Electrical potential and bridge resistance give necessary-and-sufficient full receptivity; the self-loop chain contracts in weighted mean-zero norm. Exact rational verification covered 4,294 graph/edge instances through 5 vertices, closed-form families through order 16, and 45 exact iterations. Neutral translation symmetry and unproved global limits stated.

originality.rationale: The published Kann–Feng model and a prior complete-graph result do not entail the arbitrary connected graph iff nonbridge condition and exact full-receptivity margin. Related signed BC and general resistance models differ in dynamics. Web and published-finding corpus searches found no exact coverage, subject to recorded abstract-only and bibliographic risks.
residual_risks: An obscure source could independently state this graph criterion under different names; finite query coverage never proves uniqueness.
Full text of the discrete-time sign-preserving He et al. paper was not accessible; its abstract suggests a distinct rule, but this is not a whole-document exclusion.

The electrical potential argument resembles methods of general nonlinear consensus theory; no novelty is asserted for the electrical-resistance identity in isolation, only its complete consequence for the specific strict synchronous model.

value.rationale: A single antagonistic edge is the first nontrivial structural perturbation. The result classifies every finite connected graph by whether its hostile tie has alternate contact routes, computes exact separation and strict edge activity margin through a natural invariant, and proves robustness and attraction. It distinguishes trees, cycles and cliques and supplies a graph-theoretic design criterion rather than a mere parameter substitution.
